## Domain-Driven Design

`Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.DomainDrivenDesign` — 19 patterns, 22 roles.

### Aggregate (Domain-Driven Design)

A cluster of entities and value objects treated as one unit for the purpose of data changes, with a single root that everything outside the boundary must go through.

*Eric Evans, Domain-Driven Design, 2003.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Root | `[Aggregate.Root]` | class | yes | — |
| Member | `[Aggregate.Member]` | class, struct | yes | `Root` |

**Root** — The single entity by which the aggregate is referenced from outside, and the only participant allowed to enforce the invariants that span the boundary.

**Member** — A participant living inside the boundary, reachable only through the root and never referenced by anything outside it.

Held by a subtype: yes · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/DomainDrivenDesign/Aggregate.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/DomainDrivenDesign/AggregateUsage.cs)

### AnticorruptionLayer (Domain-Driven Design)

An isolating layer through which a downstream context talks to an upstream one, so that the upstream model never reaches the downstream one.

*Eric Evans, Domain-Driven Design, 2003.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Facade | `[AnticorruptionLayer.Facade]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| Adapter | `[AnticorruptionLayer.Adapter]` | interface, class | yes | `Facade`, `Translator` |
| Translator | `[AnticorruptionLayer.Translator]` | interface, class | yes | — |

**Facade** — A simplified face over the upstream system, written in terms of the UPSTREAM model. It exists to make the upstream system easier to talk to without pretending to be anything else, so it translates nothing.

**Adapter** — What the downstream context actually calls. It exposes the protocol the downstream model expects and delegates to the facade, so that no upstream type ever appears in a downstream signature.

**Translator** — Converts between the two models, in both directions. It is the only place that knows both, which is what keeps the corruption to a single reviewable file rather than spread through the downstream model.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/DomainDrivenDesign/AnticorruptionLayer.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage.TrainOperations/AnticorruptionLayerUsage.cs)

### Assertion (Domain-Driven Design)

A post-condition of an operation or an invariant of a type, stated explicitly so that the meaning of the code is defined by its promised effect rather than recovered by reading its implementation.

*Eric Evans, Domain-Driven Design, 2003.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Assertion | `[Assertion]` | method, class, struct | yes | — |

**Assertion** — An operation whose post-condition is stated, or a type whose invariant is stated and checked rather than assumed.

Held by a subtype: yes · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/DomainDrivenDesign/Assertion.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/DomainDrivenDesign/AssertionUsage.cs)

### BoundedContext (Domain-Driven Design)

Delimits where one model applies. Inside it every term has exactly one meaning; outside it the model makes no claim at all, and the same word may name something else entirely.

*Eric Evans, Domain-Driven Design, 2003.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BoundedContext | `[BoundedContext]` | assembly | yes | — |

**BoundedContext** — The boundary of one model. Everything the assembly declares belongs to that model, and a term used here means what this model says it means — which is why a second model in the same assembly is not a boundary but a collision.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/DomainDrivenDesign/BoundedContext.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage.TrainOperations/BoundedContextUsage.cs)

### ClosureOfOperation (Domain-Driven Design)

An operation whose argument and return type are the type it is defined on, so that it stays inside its own set of values and introduces no dependency on anything else.

*Eric Evans, Domain-Driven Design, 2003.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ClosureOfOperation | `[ClosureOfOperation]` | method | no | — |

**ClosureOfOperation** — A method that takes and returns the type it is declared on, so that its results can be fed back into it without leaving the abstraction.

Held by a subtype: yes · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/DomainDrivenDesign/ClosureOfOperation.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/DomainDrivenDesign/ClosureOfOperationUsage.cs)

### ValueObject (Domain-Driven Design)

An object of the domain described only by its values. It carries no identity, it is immutable, and it exists because it says something about the domain — not merely because comparing it by value is convenient.

*Eric Evans, Domain-Driven Design, 2003.*

A narrower case of **ValueObject** (Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture): every participant here is one of those too.

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ValueObject | `[ValueObject]` | class, struct | yes | — |

**ValueObject** — An immutable object of the domain, without identity, defined only by its values.

Held by a subtype: yes · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/DomainDrivenDesign/ValueObject.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/DomainDrivenDesign/ValueObjectUsage.cs)


## Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture

`Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.EnterpriseApplicationArchitecture` — 2 patterns, 2 roles.

### UnitOfWork (Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture)

Keeps track of everything done during a business transaction that affects the store, and coordinates the writing out of the changes.

*Martin Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, 2002.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UnitOfWork | `[UnitOfWork]` | interface, class | yes | — |

**UnitOfWork** — Tracks the changes made during a business transaction, and coordinates writing them out.

Held by a subtype: yes · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/EnterpriseApplicationArchitecture/UnitOfWork.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/EnterpriseApplicationArchitecture/UnitOfWorkUsage.cs)

### ValueObject (Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture)

A small object, such as an amount of money or a date range, whose equality is not based on identity but on the values it holds, and which is therefore safe to copy and to share.

*Martin Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, 2002.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ValueObject | `[ValueObject]` | class, struct | yes | — |

**ValueObject** — An object without identity, compared by the values it holds rather than by which instance it is.

Held by a subtype: yes · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/EnterpriseApplicationArchitecture/ValueObject.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/DomainDrivenDesign/ValueObjectUsage.cs)


## Gang of Four

`Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.GangOfFour` — 23 patterns, 86 roles.

### AbstractFactory (Gang of Four)

Provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AbstractFactory | `[AbstractFactory.AbstractFactory]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteFactory | `[AbstractFactory.ConcreteFactory]` | class | yes | `AbstractFactory` |
| AbstractProduct | `[AbstractFactory.AbstractProduct]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteProduct | `[AbstractFactory.ConcreteProduct]` | class, struct | yes | `AbstractProduct` |

**AbstractFactory** — Declares the set of operations that create the abstract products of the family.

**ConcreteFactory** — Implements the creation operations for one coherent family of concrete products.

**AbstractProduct** — Declares the interface of one kind of product the family produces.

**ConcreteProduct** — Implements one abstract product, and is created by exactly one concrete factory.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/AbstractFactory.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/AbstractFactoryUsage.cs)

### Adapter (Gang of Four)

Converts the interface of a type into the interface a client expects, letting types collaborate that could not otherwise because of incompatible interfaces.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target | `[Adapter.Target]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| Adapter | `[Adapter.Adapter]` | class | yes | `Target`, `Adaptee` |
| Adaptee | `[Adapter.Adaptee]` | interface, class, struct | yes | — |

**Target** — Declares the interface the client actually uses.

**Adapter** — Implements the target interface by delegating to the adaptee and translating the calls.

**Adaptee** — Holds the behaviour worth reusing, but exposes it through an incompatible interface.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Adapter.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/AdapterUsage.cs)

### Bridge (Gang of Four)

Decouples an abstraction from its implementation so that the two can vary independently.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Abstraction | `[Bridge.Abstraction]` | class, interface | yes | `Implementor` |
| RefinedAbstraction | `[Bridge.RefinedAbstraction]` | class | yes | `Abstraction` |
| Implementor | `[Bridge.Implementor]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteImplementor | `[Bridge.ConcreteImplementor]` | class | yes | `Implementor` |

**Abstraction** — Defines the abstraction's interface and holds a reference to an implementor.

**RefinedAbstraction** — Extends the interface defined by the abstraction, without touching the implementation side.

**Implementor** — Declares the primitive operations the abstraction is built upon.

**ConcreteImplementor** — Provides one concrete implementation of the primitive operations.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Bridge.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/BridgeUsage.cs)

**Handler** — Declares the handling operation and, usually, the link to the successor.

**ConcreteHandler** — Handles the requests it is responsible for, and forwards the others to its successor.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/ChainOfResponsibility.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/ChainOfResponsibilityUsage.cs)

### Command (Gang of Four)

Encapsulates a request as an object, letting callers be parameterized with different requests, and letting requests be queued, logged or undone.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |

| Invoker | `[Command.Invoker]` | class | yes | `Command` |
| ExecuteMethod | `[Command.ExecuteMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Command** — Declares the operation that carries out the request.

**ConcreteCommand** — Binds a receiver to an action, and implements the request by invoking it.

**Receiver** — Knows how to perform the work associated with the request.

**Invoker** — Holds commands and asks them to carry out the request.

**ExecuteMethod** — The operation that carries out the request.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Command.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/CommandUsage.cs)

Composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies, and lets clients treat individual objects and compositions uniformly.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

**Leaf** — A terminal element of the tree: it has no children.

### Decorator (Gang of Four)

Attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically, as a flexible alternative to subclassing for extending behaviour.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Component | `[Decorator.Component]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteComponent | `[Decorator.ConcreteComponent]` | class | yes | `Component` |
| Decorator | `[Decorator.Decorator]` | class | yes | `Component` |
| ConcreteDecorator | `[Decorator.ConcreteDecorator]` | class | yes | `Decorator` |

**Component** — Declares the interface shared by the decorated objects and their decorators.

**ConcreteComponent** — The object to which responsibilities can be attached.

**Decorator** — Holds a component and forwards to it, providing the base for concrete decorators.

**ConcreteDecorator** — Adds one responsibility around the component it wraps.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Decorator.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/DecoratorUsage.cs)

### Facade (Gang of Four)

Provides a single, higher level interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem, making that subsystem easier to use.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Facade | `[Facade.Facade]` | class | yes | — |
| Subsystem | `[Facade.Subsystem]` | interface, class, struct | yes | — |

**Facade** — Offers the simplified entry point, and knows which subsystem type handles each request.

**Subsystem** — Does the real work, and knows nothing about the facade.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Facade.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/FacadeUsage.cs)

### FactoryMethod (Gang of Four)

Defines an interface for creating an object, but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate, deferring instantiation to them.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creator | `[FactoryMethod.Creator]` | class, interface | yes | — |
| ConcreteCreator | `[FactoryMethod.ConcreteCreator]` | class | yes | `Creator`, `ConcreteProduct` |
| Product | `[FactoryMethod.Product]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteProduct | `[FactoryMethod.ConcreteProduct]` | class, struct | yes | `Product` |
| FactoryMethod | `[FactoryMethod.FactoryMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Creator** — Declares the factory method and, usually, calls it to obtain a product.

**ConcreteCreator** — Overrides the factory method to return an instance of a concrete product.

**Product** — Declares the interface of the objects the factory method creates.

**ConcreteProduct** — Implements the product interface.

**FactoryMethod** — The operation that creates the product, and which subclasses override.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/FactoryMethod.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/FactoryMethodUsage.cs)

### Flyweight (Gang of Four)

Uses sharing to support large numbers of fine grained objects efficiently, by separating the state that can be shared from the state that cannot.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flyweight | `[Flyweight.Flyweight]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteFlyweight | `[Flyweight.ConcreteFlyweight]` | class, struct | yes | `Flyweight` |
| UnsharedConcreteFlyweight | `[Flyweight.UnsharedConcreteFlyweight]` | class, struct | yes | `Flyweight` |
| FlyweightFactory | `[Flyweight.FlyweightFactory]` | class | yes | `Flyweight` |

**Flyweight** — Declares the operations through which flyweights receive the state that is not shared.

**ConcreteFlyweight** — A shareable flyweight: it holds only state that is independent of its context.

**UnsharedConcreteFlyweight** — A flyweight that is deliberately not shared, although the interface allows sharing.

**FlyweightFactory** — Creates and manages flyweights, and guarantees that shared ones are reused.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Flyweight.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/FlyweightUsage.cs)

### Interpreter (Gang of Four)

Given a language, defines a representation for its grammar together with an interpreter that uses that representation to interpret sentences of the language.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AbstractExpression | `[Interpreter.AbstractExpression]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| TerminalExpression | `[Interpreter.TerminalExpression]` | class, struct | yes | `AbstractExpression` |
| NonterminalExpression | `[Interpreter.NonterminalExpression]` | class | yes | `AbstractExpression` |
| Context | `[Interpreter.Context]` | class, struct | yes | — |

**AbstractExpression** — Declares the interpretation operation shared by every node of the syntax tree.

**TerminalExpression** — Interprets a terminal symbol of the grammar: it has no sub expression.

**NonterminalExpression** — Interprets a grammar rule by delegating to its sub expressions.

**Context** — Carries the information global to the interpretation.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Interpreter.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/InterpreterUsage.cs)

### Iterator (Gang of Four)

Provides a way to access the elements of an aggregate object sequentially, without exposing its underlying representation.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Iterator | `[Iterator.Iterator]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteIterator | `[Iterator.ConcreteIterator]` | class, struct | yes | `Iterator`, `ConcreteAggregate` |
| Aggregate | `[Iterator.Aggregate]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteAggregate | `[Iterator.ConcreteAggregate]` | class | yes | `Aggregate` |

**Iterator** — Declares the operations for traversing the elements.

**ConcreteIterator** — Implements the traversal, and keeps track of the current position.

**Aggregate** — Declares the operation that creates an iterator over its elements.

**ConcreteAggregate** — Returns an iterator suited to its own representation.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Iterator.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/IteratorUsage.cs)

### Mediator (Gang of Four)

Defines an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact, keeping them from referring to each other explicitly.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mediator | `[Mediator.Mediator]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteMediator | `[Mediator.ConcreteMediator]` | class | yes | `Mediator` |
| Colleague | `[Mediator.Colleague]` | interface, class | yes | `Mediator` |
| ConcreteColleague | `[Mediator.ConcreteColleague]` | class | yes | `Colleague` |

**Mediator** — Declares the interface through which colleagues communicate.

**ConcreteMediator** — Knows the colleagues and coordinates their interactions.

**Colleague** — Communicates with the other participants only through the mediator.

**ConcreteColleague** — One participant of the interaction.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Mediator.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/MediatorUsage.cs)

### Memento (Gang of Four)

Captures and externalizes an object's internal state, without violating encapsulation, so that the object can be restored to that state later.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Originator | `[Memento.Originator]` | class | yes | `Memento` |
| Memento | `[Memento.Memento]` | class, struct | yes | — |
| Caretaker | `[Memento.Caretaker]` | class | yes | `Memento` |

**Originator** — Creates a memento of its own state, and uses one to restore itself.

**Memento** — Holds the captured state, and exposes it only to its originator.

**Caretaker** — Keeps mementos safe, and never inspects or alters their content.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Memento.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/MementoUsage.cs)

### Observer (Gang of Four)

Defines a one to many dependency between objects, so that when one object changes state all its dependents are notified and updated automatically.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Subject | `[Observer.Subject]` | interface, class | yes | `Observer` |
| ConcreteSubject | `[Observer.ConcreteSubject]` | class | yes | `Subject` |
| Observer | `[Observer.Observer]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteObserver | `[Observer.ConcreteObserver]` | class | yes | `Observer`, `ConcreteSubject` |
| NotifyMethod | `[Observer.NotifyMethod]` | method | no | — |
| UpdateMethod | `[Observer.UpdateMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Subject** — Knows its observers, and declares the operations to attach and detach them.

**ConcreteSubject** — Holds the state of interest, and notifies its observers when it changes.

**Observer** — Declares the update operation invoked when the observed subject changes.

**ConcreteObserver** — Reacts to the notification, and keeps itself consistent with the subject.

**NotifyMethod** — The operation that informs every registered observer of a change.

**UpdateMethod** — The operation invoked on an observer when the subject has changed.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Observer.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/ObserverUsage.cs)

### Prototype (Gang of Four)

Specifies the kinds of objects to create using a prototypical instance, and creates new objects by copying that prototype.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prototype | `[Prototype.Prototype]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcretePrototype | `[Prototype.ConcretePrototype]` | class, struct | yes | `Prototype` |
| CloneMethod | `[Prototype.CloneMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Prototype** — Declares the operation that clones itself.

**ConcretePrototype** — Implements the cloning operation for its own representation.

**CloneMethod** — The operation that returns a copy of the prototype.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Prototype.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/PrototypeUsage.cs)

### Proxy (Gang of Four)

Provides a surrogate or placeholder for another object in order to control access to it.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Subject | `[Proxy.Subject]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| RealSubject | `[Proxy.RealSubject]` | class | yes | `Subject` |
| Proxy | `[Proxy.Proxy]` | class | yes | `Subject`, `RealSubject` |

**Subject** — Declares the interface shared by the real object and its proxy, so that they are interchangeable.

**RealSubject** — The object the proxy stands for, and which does the real work.

**Proxy** — Controls access to the real subject, and may be responsible for creating it.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Proxy.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/ProxyUsage.cs)

### Singleton (Gang of Four)

Ensures a type has only one instance, and provides a global point of access to it.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Singleton | `[Singleton]` | class | yes | — |

**Singleton** — Ensures a type has only one instance, and provides a global point of access to it.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Singleton.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/SingletonUsage.cs)

### State (Gang of Four)

Lets an object alter its behaviour when its internal state changes, so that it appears to change its class.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Context | `[State.Context]` | class | yes | `State` |
| State | `[State.State]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteState | `[State.ConcreteState]` | class, struct | yes | `State` |

**Context** — Holds the current state, and delegates the state dependent behaviour to it.

**State** — Declares the behaviour that varies with the state of the context.

**ConcreteState** — Implements the behaviour associated with one state of the context.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/State.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/StateUsage.cs)

### Strategy (Gang of Four)

Defines a family of interchangeable algorithms, encapsulates each one, and lets the algorithm vary independently from the clients that use it.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Context | `[Strategy.Context]` | class | yes | `Strategy` |
| Strategy | `[Strategy.Strategy]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteStrategy | `[Strategy.ConcreteStrategy]` | class, struct | yes | `Strategy` |

**Context** — Is configured with a strategy, and delegates the algorithm to it.

**Strategy** — Declares the interface common to every supported algorithm.

**ConcreteStrategy** — Implements one algorithm behind the strategy interface.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Strategy.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/StrategyUsage.cs)

### TemplateMethod (Gang of Four)

Defines the skeleton of an algorithm in an operation, deferring some steps to subclasses so they can redefine them without changing the algorithm's structure.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AbstractClass | `[TemplateMethod.AbstractClass]` | class | yes | — |
| ConcreteClass | `[TemplateMethod.ConcreteClass]` | class | yes | `AbstractClass` |
| TemplateMethod | `[TemplateMethod.TemplateMethod]` | method | no | — |
| PrimitiveOperation | `[TemplateMethod.PrimitiveOperation]` | method | no | — |
| HookOperation | `[TemplateMethod.HookOperation]` | method | no | — |

**AbstractClass** — Defines the skeleton of the algorithm, and declares the steps subclasses must supply.

**ConcreteClass** — Supplies the steps the algorithm defers to subclasses.

**TemplateMethod** — The operation that holds the skeleton of the algorithm, and calls the deferred steps.

**PrimitiveOperation** — A step the algorithm defers, and which subclasses must supply.

**HookOperation** — A step the algorithm defers, and which subclasses may override, but need not.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/TemplateMethod.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/TemplateMethodUsage.cs)

### Visitor (Gang of Four)

Represents an operation to be performed on the elements of an object structure, and lets a new operation be defined without changing the classes of those elements.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Visitor | `[Visitor.Visitor]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteVisitor | `[Visitor.ConcreteVisitor]` | class | yes | `Visitor` |
| Element | `[Visitor.Element]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteElement | `[Visitor.ConcreteElement]` | class, struct | yes | `Element` |
| ObjectStructure | `[Visitor.ObjectStructure]` | class | yes | `Element` |
| VisitMethod | `[Visitor.VisitMethod]` | method | no | `ConcreteElement` |
| AcceptMethod | `[Visitor.AcceptMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Visitor** — Declares one visit operation per concrete element of the structure.

**ConcreteVisitor** — Implements the visit operations: this is where the added algorithm lives.

**Element** — Declares the entry point of the double dispatch.

**ConcreteElement** — Dispatches to the visit operation that corresponds to its own type.

**ObjectStructure** — Holds the elements, and offers a way to walk them.

**VisitMethod** — The operation applied to one given concrete element.

**AcceptMethod** — The entry point of the double dispatch: it calls back the matching visit operation.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Visitor.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/VisitorUsage.cs)
